messages:
maya (support): hey team, incoming from a customer — hosted inference API returning a bunch of 5xx for their traffic starting ~11:02 UTC. customer says errors are 502/504 gateway + empty bodies. they sent example request IDs: req-9a1c2f, req-9a1c3b, req-9a1c7d. they repro by hitting /v1/infer with fairly small payloads, not heavy. can someone triage? :warning:

jon (sre): on it. which region + model? any correlation with deployments?

maya (support): region=us-west-2, model pinned to rwd-13b-v2, no deploys from customer side. internal deploys list shows a routing-policy change around 11:00 from kevin's team (small config tweak). attaching customer cURL:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/infer```

kevin (eng-platform): that routing-policy change was a config toggle to enable more strict tenant routing (feature flag). i rolled that at 10:58. pushing to rollback now but will need a few minutes to propagate.

deploy-bot: rollback job started for routing-policy-service, job id rp-rollback-772. logs: tailing...

jon (sre): gathering control-plane logs. initial look: spike in routing-policy service latency at 10:59 -> 11:05. upstream configdb timeout errors in logs: `GET /tenants/config 504 (timeout)` repeated, connection pool reported saturated. routing-policy then returned 502 to control-plane, which bubbled to gateway as 502. saving snippets:```[11:01:03] routing-policy ERROR timeout fetching config for tenant=acct-54321: timeout after 3s``````[11:02:10] configdb WARN pool exhausted: waiting=45 active=200 max=200``````[11:03:22] controlplane WARN fallback not available, returning 502`````` request ids req-9a1c2f matched these timestamps.```

kevin (eng-platform): thanks. pool max=200 is what we set for configdb in us-west-2 recently; looks like sudden fanout from many control-plane requests after routing-policy strictness increased. i can patch to increase pool + add short circuit to serve cached routing policy for 30s if configdb slow.

sophie (customer): FYI our error rates went from 0.2% to ~18% within minutes. we have production traffic — this is blocking. any ETA?

jon (sre): immediate mitigations: 1) rollback of the routing-policy toggle (deploy-bot shows completion at 11:07), 2) temporarily increase configdb connection pool and reduce request fanout by adding a 100ms jitter/backoff to control-plane callers. roll executed: rp-rollback-772 -> success.

kevin (eng-platform): rolled rollback at 11:07, bumped pool to 300 at 11:09. also deployed a runtime guard to return cached policy on configdb timeouts for up to 15s at 11:11 (can revert later).

jon (sre): monitoring now. CPU on routing-policy returned to baseline by 11:15, 5xx rate dropped to normal by 11:18. correlating graphs: error spike started 11:00, peaked 11:03, recovered by 11:18. attaching perf snippet link: https://grafana.redwood/shot/xyz (internal).

maya (support): passed mitigation notes to customer (sophie). sent repro guidance: ask them to retry requests, and we recommended they implement exponential backoff 429/5xx -> retry with jitter. sophie, can you confirm if your traffic normalized after ~11:20?

sophie (customer): we've seen success rate return to >99% after 11:20, thanks. we still saw a couple of timeouts around 11:30, but much better. please follow up with root cause and plan to avoid recurrence.

jon (sre): root cause summary (for ticket): routing-policy strictness toggle increased per-request fanout to configdb (more tenants hit configdb for policy check). configdb hit max connections -> pool exhaustion -> timeouts -> routing-policy returned 502/504 -> control-plane surfaced 5xx -> gateway returned to client. contributing factors: aggressive pool sizing post-recent infra change, no short-circuit cache when configdb misbehaves, and no gradual rollout for routing-policy toggle.

kevin (eng-platform): action items: (1) add circuit-breaker with cached fallback for routing-policy (short TTL) — done as emergency patch (monitor for false positives), (2) increase configdb pool cap and add autoscaling for connection workers, (3) add rollout gating for routing-policy toggles (canary 1% -> 10% -> 100%), (4) add alerting for pool saturation (already creating alert). i'll open PRs/infra tickets and include owners.

jon (sre): I'll file postmortem ticket and link the graphs + logs + request ids. also want to run a chaos test to ensure cached fallback behaves under sustained configdb failure.

maya (support): logged incident with customer-facing summary and next steps. sophie, we will share a postmortem and expected timetable for infra fixes within 48 hours.

sophie (customer): appreciate quick response. please cc our ops contact on the postmortem: ops+accts@customerco.com.

kevin (eng-platform): noted, will cc. posting initial PR links: https://git.redwood/repo/routing-policy/pulls/321 (emergency fallback), https://git.redwood/repo/configdb/issues/88 (pool/autoscale).

jon (sre): closing triage thread, follow-ups will be in INCIDENT-2026-07-rp-configdb-fanout. tagging @oncall for 24h watch. :white_check_mark:
